system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Buyer-side analysis only.

---

## 0. Threshold points before the clause-by-clause review

**The "FINAL / agreed / market standard" preamble has no effect on our position.** The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "standard and widely accepted market terms" and are "not intended to be re-opened". Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, we treat none of this as agreed:

- **No buyer-side authority exists.** Our records show no approval from Amelia Frost for any concession: not the 20% cap, not the 18-month period, not anything else. A counterparty's statement that something was agreed does not make it agreed.
- **"Market standard" is advocacy.** Even if a market range existed, it would not override our playbook.

**Recommendation:** Reply in writing that Wattlebridge does not accept that any position is final or pre-agreed. Ask the Seller to identify who it says agreed, when, and in what document. If anyone on our side has had principal-level discussions, confirm them internally through Amelia Frost before responding on substance.

**The Seller Update contradicts its own Disclosure Letter.**

| Topic | Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | Consent is "addressed" | No final consent and no evidence of conditions (DL para 2) |
| Riverlark | Will be "addressed" | Facility not repaid, no discharge (DL para 3) |
| Ironquay | Indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment (DL para 4) |

We should rely on the more specific disclosures and treat the Update's characterisations as assertions.

**The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Before we settle any position, we should request a bring-down on each of the following:

- Bluefen consent status
- Riverlark payout
- Ironquay payment
- DD-006 investigation
- Bonus status
- Sandbar renewals

We should distinguish verified updates from new assertions.

**There is a numbering gap.** The Disclosure Letter jumps from para 1.2 to 1.4. Ask the Seller to confirm whether a para 1.3 exists or was deleted, and to provide the full text.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m. Reject.

- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Why the matching number does not help:** 20% is our conditional fallback, but it is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. None has been given. A proposal is not cleared because one number happens to match a fallback.
- **The rest of the package makes it worse.** The 20% cap comes with:
  - a 5x larger basket
  - a tipping-to-deductible mechanism
  - a shorter claims period
  - no fundamental carve-out
  - no fraud carve-out

  Taken together, the effective protection is far below what a 20% cap would normally give.
- **Response:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal the fallback.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2). Reject.

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 (~1% of price) | AUD 50,000 |
| Mechanism | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar once exceeded) |

The deductible structure alone permanently writes off AUD 250,000 of valid claims. The high de minimis would also exclude many realistic SaaS warranty claims, such as individual contract, privacy or IP items.

**Response:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

### 1.3 Claims period (cl 12.3 / 13). Reject.

- **Period:** 18 months is our fallback and needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Our position is 24 months after Completion.
- **The second sentence is a hidden override.** It says "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". This flips the default so that general limitations sweep in Title, Capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants and fraud, unless each is carved out by express words. That is the general-regime override the playbook prohibits.
- **Response:** delete the second sentence. Limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims as defined. Each other category should have its own express regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties. Reject.

- **Seller position:** subject capacity and title to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Why this matters:** title is the asset we are buying. If title fails, our loss is up to the full AUD 24m price, but recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window.
- **Playbook position:**
  - separate regime
  - 100% cap
  - at least six years
  - outside the basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). Reject. This is the most serious drafting issue.

- **No fraud carve-out.** Read with cl 12.3's "applies to all Claims", this would purport to cap, time-bar and exclude reliance-based claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Playbook position:** these must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable. No one on our side can concede it, including in exchange for other movement.
- **Why "the law protects us anyway" is not enough:** courts may decline to enforce fraud exclusions. We should still not accept drafting that invites argument. Non-reliance clauses in particular can be deployed against misleading-conduct claims.
- **Response:** insert an express, overriding carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers, employees, agents and advisers. Confine exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language so that it does not extend to these matters, title, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Schedule 7; DL paras 1.1–1.2). Reject.

- **What the Seller is claiming:** "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the entire data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Why this is unacceptable:** this is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects.
  - "Referred to" extends disclosure to documents not even in the data room.
  - "Publicly searchable" is effectively prudent-search disclosure.
- **Response:**
  - Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Only specific disclosures, made with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the relevant warranty, should qualify the warranties.
  - Disclosure should never qualify Title, Capacity or the specific indemnities.

### 2.2 DL para 1.4 (no admissions)

A no-admission statement is not unusual in itself, but its scope needs controlling.

- **Response:** accept it only if it is clarified that it does not dilute any warranty, condition precedent or indemnity. It also cannot convert open matters into "not required". For example, whether Bluefen consent or DD-006 notification is legally required remains an open question for us to determine.

### 2.3 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). Reject and delete.

- **What it does:** bars claims for anything known to the Buyer "or its advisers", including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Combined with the general disclosure, this would neutralise most warranties. It would arguably also bar claims on matters we have specifically identified and negotiated protection for, such as Ironquay, DD-006 and Bluefen.
- **Playbook position:** delete the blanket exclusion.
- **If any qualifier is ever discussed, it must:**
  - relate to the *Seller's* knowledge, with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity

  Constructive "discoverable" knowledge is not acceptable in any form.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3). Reject.

- **Why it is material:** DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%), with change-control consent under cl 11.2 and conditions under cl 11.3. That makes it a material customer consent.
- **Problems with the Seller's proposal:**
  1. "Reasonable endeavours" is insufficient for a material customer consent.
  2. "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is consent-on-delivery. It ignores whether the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, so a conditional consent could be "delivered" and still be ineffective.
  3. The Update says the matter is "addressed", but DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of conditions as at 22 September.
- **Response:**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, together with evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
  - Require the CP in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, with procurement obligations and information rights.
  - Request a current status update.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7). Reject.

- **Seller position:** the facility (about AUD 3.2m, change-control cl 8.1, discharge cl 9.2) "will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion". DL para 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- **Risk:** the change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1, and security would remain over the Company's assets after we own it.
- **Playbook position:**
  - a current payout letter
  - direct repayment from Completion funds
  - executed, effective security releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion
- **A post-completion release** is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is offered or in place.
- **Price mechanics:** confirm the payout is treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free calculation, so the price is not paid twice.

### 3.3 Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses. Reject.

- **Seller position:** the AUD 420,000 bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised". DL para 5 confirms they do not appear in the funds flow, and the Seller does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Why this is a problem:** the bonuses are triggered by Completion and will likely be paid by the Company, which will be ours. If they are not deducted, we bear the cost silently. That is exactly the exclusion the playbook prohibits.
- **Response:**
  - Either include the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific Debt or Transaction Cost line item deducted from the price, or have them funded directly by the Seller at Completion.
  - Back this with an indemnity for any shortfall or later-assessed on-costs.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation and whether the continued-employment conditions mean any amounts could fall due after Completion.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). Push back.

- **Facts:**
  - DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but DL para 4 itself says this is not independent verification.
  - There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Why the indemnity is inadequate:** limiting it to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the fee. It does not cover our real exposure:
  - failure of IP ownership in the Project Materials
  - infringement claims
  - costs of re-development or licensing
  - business disruption
- **Response:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold an unencumbered right to use, the Ironquay deliverables.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: at or before Completion, cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.
- **The amount:** do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed in either direction. Ask for bank-verified evidence of the amount actually outstanding.

### 4.2 DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6). Push back on the characterisation.

- **Seller position:** "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". That is an unsupported assertion.
- **What DL para 6 actually says:** a download link went to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification obligations are all unestablished.
- **Our discipline:** we should not overstate it either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss.
- **Response (protective, not accusatory):**
  - **Preservation:** a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence.
  - **Investigation:** completion of the investigation, ideally with independent forensic input.
  - **Information rights:** regular written updates before Completion, plus Buyer consultation and approval rights over any notification or regulator engagement decisions.
  - **Indemnity:** a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limits.
  - **Disclosure:** confirmation that the incident disclosure does not qualify the privacy and data warranties beyond what is actually known.
  - **Bring-down:** a bring-down warranty as at Completion.

  Do not make any numeric demand until facts are established.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000). Assess. Do not accept the Seller's characterisation.

- **Seller position:** "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **What DL para 8 actually says:** it does *not* state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. It also asks that DD-008 and DD-011 be read together for timing and scope, which suggests possible splitting or a related arrangement.
- **Playbook position:** no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Response:**
  - Request the three agreements, approval records and accounting treatment.
  - Determine whether they are ordinary course, pre-paid or accrued, terminable, or entered into outside the conduct-of-business covenants.
  - Decide the treatment once the facts are known.

### 4.4 Office lease (DL para 7) and Mossvale (DL para 9). Verify.

- **What the Seller says:** the lease contains a notification obligation, and Mossvale contains an assignment restriction. The Seller frames neither as requiring consent to the share sale.
- **Our position:** that may be right, but we should verify ourselves rather than rely on the Seller's framing.
- **Response:**
  - Have the provisions reviewed, including any change-of-control-as-assignment deeming language.
  - If notification is needed, add it as a pre-Completion or Completion deliverable.

### 4.5 Tax and IP warranties. Not settled.

- **Seller position:** these are "settled under the general regime".
- **Playbook position:** both remain open. That is also a backdoor route to the general-regime override discussed at 1.3.
- **Response:**
  - Reserve our position and keep Tax and IP as separate categories (with Tax handled via a tax indemnity or deed).
  - Do not assume they are resolved.
  - Do not assume they carry unlimited liability. Negotiate them on their own terms.

### 4.6 Title evidence. Not sufficient.

- **What the Seller offers:** the DD-012 share register. DL para 10 itself concedes this is the Seller's source and not Buyer verification.
- **Response:** require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract cross-checked against the register
  - share issue and transfer history, with supporting resolutions and stamping where relevant
  - share certificates, or confirmation that none exist
  - PPSR search over the shares and the Seller
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or other rights to shares
  - Seller authority documents (board resolution and evidence of capacity)
  - releases of any encumbrance over the shares

  Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime regardless of this evidence.

---

## 5. Category separation

Several provisions work together to collapse every category into the general regime:

- cl 12.3's "applies to all Claims"
- cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 "all Claims of any nature"
- the Title proposal
- the "Tax/IP settled under general regime" statement

In the mark-up, define and keep separate:

1. **General Warranty Claims:** general cap, basket and period.
2. **Fundamental / Title / Capacity:** 100%, at least six years, no basket or knowledge bar.
3. **Tax:** separate, open.
4. **IP / specific indemnities:** Ironquay, DD-006 and bonuses, outside general limits.
5. **Payment obligations:** price adjustment and leakage.
6. **Covenants:** restraint, confidentiality and conduct of business.
7. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct:** outside everything.

Add an express clause that general limitations apply *only* to General Warranty Claims unless the SPA expressly states otherwise. That reverses the Seller's default.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / agreed / market" | Not to be re-opened | Reject. No buyer authority. Ask for the basis. Confirm internally via Amelia Frost. |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m. Fallback is not authorised. |
| 3 | De minimis / basket | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar once exceeded |
| 4 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months. Delete "applies to all Claims". |
| 5 | Title / Capacity | General limits | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out. Limits, non-reliance and exclusive remedy apply to "all Claims". | Full carve-out from everything. Non-negotiable. |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room, registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only. Delete DL 1.1–1.2. Clarify 1.4. Ask about the missing 1.3. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Buyer and advisers, actual and "discoverable" | Delete. Any qualifier only on named Seller knowledge persons plus enquiry. |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | Effective consent plus evidence cl 11.3 conditions are met, as a CP before Completion. Stronger endeavours. |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded, with indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | Broaden to IP ownership loss. Keep SOW3 cure (payment plus assignment). Verify AUD 180k. |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation, updates, consultation rights, specific indemnity. No assumptions either way. |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Diligence first. No automatic Debt treatment. |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify independently. Add any notice as a deliverable. |
| 16 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | Open. Separate categories. |
| 17 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, history, authority) |
| 18 | Stale facts | As at 22 September 2026 | Request bring-down on all open items as at today |

**Suggested next steps:**

1. Send a holding response rejecting the "final" characterisation and requesting the bring-down information.
2. Escalate to Amelia Frost, to confirm no prior concessions were made and to decide whether any fallback authority will be given. Until she gives written authority identifying this draft, we hold the starting positions.
3. Prepare the full SPA mark-up on the basis above, prioritising items 6 (fraud), 5 (title), 9–11 (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) and the category-separation drafting. These carry the largest uncapped or price-level exposure.
=== END ADVICE ===
